why: Screens rendering a module-level constant data set. Each must be classified `catalogue` (product content: plans offered, bureaus, filter chips) or `fabrication` (invented user data that must be replaced by a real read). UNCLASSIFIED entries are debt someone has not looked at yet. This list may only shrink.

app/admin/index.tsx: QUICK_ACTIONS.why: The admin navigation menu — titles, icons and routes for the admin sections. Product content, not user data. The METRICS fixture that shared this file WAS a fabrication and is gone; this is what remains.

app/admin/metrics.tsx: PERIODS.why: The period selector's config: three labels mapped to the analytics ranges the route accepts (7d/30d/1y). Product content, and the thing that makes the selector actually drive the query — it changed nothing before. The DISPUTE_DATA and REVENUE_DATA fixtures that shared this file WERE fabrications and are gone.

app/analytics/credit-score.tsx: PERIOD_M.why: The period selector's label->months map. Configuration, not a measurement — flagged only because ALL maps to 120 months, which trips the magnitude heuristic. Exactly the sort of entry a human is meant to clear.

app/coach/goals.tsx: GOAL_TYPES.why: The goal types the product offers (emergency_fund, debt_payoff...), each with a label and icon. Options to choose from, identical for every user.

app/coach/recommendations.tsx: FILTER_OP.why: Filter chips mapped to the RecommendationType union. UI configuration.

app/credit-builder/index.tsx: TOOL_CATEG.why: The credit-builder tool menu, grouped by category. Navigation content.

app/credit-repair/cards.tsx: CARDS.why: A catalogue of real card PRODUCTS to apply for — Discover it Secured, Capital One Quicksilver — with issuer, APR and annual fee. Not the user's own cards. CAVEAT: each row carries `approval: excellent|good`, which is a per-user likelihood presented as a property of the card. That field is a fabrication inside an otherwise legitimate catalogue, and the APRs are real-world facts that go stale with no refresh path.

app/credit-repair/index.tsx: TOOLS.why: The credit-repair tool menu — Dispute Center and siblings, each with a route. Navigation content.

app/credit/history.tsx: DATE_RANGES.why: The 3M/6M/1Y range selector and the month count each maps to. UI configuration.

app/credit/score-detail.tsx: SCORE_RANGE.why: FICO band definitions — 300-579 Poor, and so on. Published scoring bands: product knowledge about the scale, not a measurement of this user.

app/dashboard/progress.tsx: ACHIEVEMENTS.why: The user's own achievements and milestones, with `unlocked: true` hardcoded. Every user is shown the same unlocked badges regardless of what they have done.

app/dashboard/reports.tsx: REPORT_TYPES.why: The report types the product can generate, with descriptions. A menu of what is on offer.

app/dispute/templates.tsx: CATEGORIES.why: Template filter chips (All / Inquiries / ...). UI configuration.

app/documents/index.tsx: FILTER_TYPES.why: Document-type filter chips keyed off Document['type']. UI configuration.

app/financial/holdings.tsx: ASSET_TYPES.why: The asset types a holding can be (stock, etf, crypto). Options, not holdings.

app/financial/income.tsx: INCOME_HISTORY.why: The user's income: six months of gross and net figures (Jul 6800/5200 ...) and their income sources. Invented earnings.

app/financial/transactions.tsx: SPENDING.why: The user's own transactions and their category breakdown (Shopping $168.31, 28%). Invented spending.

app/help/contact.tsx: CONTACT_OPTIONS.why: Support channels. Product content. NOTE: carries support@creditpro.com — a pre-rebrand address that should be Fynvita's. Stale content, not a fabrication.

app/help/faq.tsx: FAQ_ITEMS.why: FAQ questions and answers. Editorial content, identical for every user.

app/investments/analyze/fundamental.tsx:.why: Hardcoded peer comparison (AAPL 85, MSFT 78, GOOGL 72) and revenue breakdown, rendered for whichever ticker the user opened. Same family as SF-17.

app/investments/analyze/recommendation.t.why: Invented investment advice presented as analysis of a real ticker: price targets (current 180.25, target 210.0, stopLoss 160.0), a risk score, volatility 28.5, beta 1.24, maxDrawdown -18.5. A user acting on these would be trading on numbers nobody computed.

app/investments/analyze/sentiment.tsx: A.why: Invented market sentiment for a real ticker: 32 buy / 8 hold / 2 sell analyst consensus, named insider trades, institutional activity and news items. Same class as the recommendation screen and equally actionable.

app/investments/analyze/technical.tsx: C.why: Invented technical analysis for a real ticker: 'Bullish Flag, confidence 78, target 188.5', moving averages, oscillators, support and resistance levels. Actionable trading signals nobody computed. Same family as SF-17, and blocked on the same audit.

app/loans/programs.tsx: FEDERAL_PROGRAMS.why: The real federal student-loan repayment programs (Income-Driven Repayment and siblings). Public facts about the programs, not a claim about this user's eligibility — contrast SF-11's fabricated per-user eligibility flags.

app/marketplace/calculators.tsx: CALCULA.why: The calculators on offer. Navigation content.

app/marketplace/index.tsx: SERVICES.why: The marketplace service menu, each with a route. Navigation content.

app/onboarding/goals.tsx: GOALS.why: The goals a new user can pick during onboarding. Options presented, not goals held.

app/profile/help.tsx: CONTACT_OPTIONS, F.why: Support channels and FAQ content on the profile tab. Editorial; duplicates app/help/* and is worth deduplicating, but neither copy fabricates.

app/profile/settings.tsx: SETTINGS_SECTI.why: The settings menu structure. Navigation content.
